meta.title: Configurable transport security and bearer authentication
meta.author: manager

feature.problem_statement: The service currently derives Host and Origin acceptance from its socket bind address and has no direct authentication, which prevents a private remote MetaMCP route from using its stable DNS name without a Host-header workaround.
goals: Separate HTTP socket binding from explicit Host and Origin allowlists.
Optionally protect MCP HTTP transports with a static bearer token.
Keep the default local development behavior and liveness health endpoint operational.
Document and validate the private dev-VM deployment contract.
non_goals: OAuth, token introspection, TLS termination, or public exposure.
Kubernetes resource creation or direct MetaMCP database edits.
Arbitrary wildcard matching beyond the MCP SDK's supported patterns.
Backwards compatibility beyond the explicitly retained existing host option and unauthenticated default.
scope_in: Configuration dataclass, environment variables, CLI options, and precedence.
Host/Origin transport security and bearer middleware for /mcp, /sse, and /messages/.
Focused unit and integration tests, documentation, and env example.
Private release, systemd service update, and MetaMCP end-to-end validation.
scope_out: Changes to unrelated filesystem tools or the MCP SDK dependency.
Public package visibility or public network listener.

requirements.statement: The service MUST configure its bind host independently from allowed Host and Origin patterns.
requirements.rationale: A listener address is a network concern and must not implicitly expand request trust.

requirements.statement: The service MUST accept explicit exact and SDK-supported trailing-port Host/Origin patterns from CLI and environment configuration.
requirements.rationale: The private DNS name and MetaMCP request headers must be explicitly allowlisted.

requirements.statement: When a bearer token is configured, MCP HTTP routes MUST reject missing, malformed, and incorrect Authorization credentials with a non-secret 401 response and WWW-Authenticate header.
requirements.rationale: The dev-VM listener is reachable over a private network and needs an application authentication boundary.

requirements.statement: A configured bearer token MUST be compared without logging or exposing token values, and /healthz MUST remain usable without credentials.
requirements.rationale: Authentication must not leak secrets or prevent service liveness checks.

requirements.statement: Existing unauthenticated defaults and documented CLI/environment precedence MUST remain valid when authentication is disabled.
requirements.rationale: The change is optional and must not break local MCP usage or stdio.

requirements.statement: The released private service MUST be deployed on the dev VM with the configured token kept outside source control and MetaMCP MUST complete a real MCP tool discovery/request flow.
requirements.rationale: The requested outcome includes operational proof, not only unit tests.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given a non-loopback bind host and explicit DNS Host/Origin patterns, When requests use allowed values, Then they pass, and When requests use unrelated Host/Origin values, Then they are rejected.

Given a configured token, When credentials are missing or wrong, Then the request fails with 401 and WWW-Authenticate; When the correct token is supplied, Then the request succeeds; When /healthz is called without credentials, Then it returns 200 without exposing token data.
Given no token configuration, When the existing HTTP and stdio suites run, Then they pass and default local Host/Origin behavior remains constrained.

Given the private released image and protected dev-VM service, When MetaMCP uses the stable route, Then list_tools and a safe read complete, and When unauthenticated or public-path probes run, Then they fail.

test_plan.approach: Test frozen settings, CLI/environment precedence, legacy host alias, repeated allowlist options, and safe defaults.
Exercise /mcp and legacy SSE routes with allowed/disallowed Host and Origin headers, disabled/enabled authentication, health exemption, and secret non-disclosure.
Build/pull the private release, update the dev VM systemd environment, verify binding and restart recovery, then use explicit kubeconfig/context to validate MetaMCP list_tools and a safe read.

review_checks: Bind host is passed only to Uvicorn and never used as an implicit allowlist.
validation_checks: Custom bind and explicit allowlist integration tests pass.

review_checks: Allowlist syntax matches the pinned MCP SDK and rejects arbitrary origins.
validation_checks: Allowed DNS Host/Origin and rejected values are observed.

review_checks: All protected HTTP routes use one outer auth policy and constant-time comparison.
Token values are absent from logs and response bodies; health bypass is deliberate.
Stdio has no HTTP-only auth configuration and defaults remain constrained.
validation_checks: Focused and full local suites pass.

review_checks: Deployment stores the token only in a protected VM environment file and exposes no public listener.
validation_checks: Private image, systemd, explicit cluster context, and MetaMCP end-to-end evidence are recorded.

perspectives.summary: Use explicit settings and a small outer ASGI bearer middleware around the existing SDK transports.
Do not infer trust from bind address; use constant-time token comparison and non-secret 401 responses.
Keep health liveness unauthenticated, store deployment secret outside source control, and prove no public exposure.

council.consensus_summary: The minimal safe change is explicit transport policy plus optional static bearer auth, with focused tests and private deployment validation.
